newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia deports remaining Timor meeting activists.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia deports remaining Timor meeting activists.

text.p: Malaysia deported on Monday the remaining 10 foreign activists who participated in a controversial conference on East Timor, the immigration department said.
All were Filipinos, an immigration department spokesperson at the Kuala Lumpur international airport said.
"Nine are on flight MH 704 to Manila and one is on SQ 105 to Singapore for a connecting flight to Manila," she said.
Thirty-six foreign activists were expelled on Sunday.
They included two Roman Catholic bishops -- Aloisuis Nobuo Somo of Nagoya, Japan and Hilton Deakin of Melbourne, Australia.

The foreigners along with dozens of Malaysian activists and two foreign journalists were detained after the meeting was disrupted by a youth group which stormed into it shouting slogans and singing patriotic songs.

On Sunday, the police freed 26 local activists and the Singapore-based correspondent of the Australia Broadcasting Corporation, Catherine McGrath, on personal bonds. Others, including Asiaweek's correspondent in Kuala Lumpur, Roger Mitton, are expected to be released by Wednesday, lawyers for the activists said.
